description: Read-only access to the point-in-time Longbridge archive (#2575): the capture's health, and archived values as of a past moment. The capture runs outside Neige as a systemd timer; this plugin only reads the archive and the capture's last exit, never the token, and never calls Longbridge.
planner_instructions: The archive plugin reports the health of the Longbridge archive capture, a systemd timer outside Neige; nothing here captures or changes the archive. plugin_archive_capture_status answers ok, attention or failing, with every reason and the recent runs. failing means a person has to act on the host (a lost day stays failing until a later day ends complete): ask the owner with neige_user_ask, one question quoting the reasons, and ask again only when the reasons change. attention means data was lost or is weaker than planned: say so in the Report, without asking. plugin_archive_capture_watch with on: true keeps this Track's live archive.status table, which the Report shows with a table block whose source is neige://plugin/archive/archive.status; on: false removes it. plugin_archive_read_at answers what the archive held at a past moment `at`: per symbol and endpoint, the latest successful fetch at or before `at`, narrowed by a JSON pointer. Use it for where consensus, ratings or target prices stood at a time, and call it twice to compare two times. The original six endpoints began capture on 2026-10-13 (UTC), for trading day 2026-10-12. Annual consensus starts only after its own first planned capture; never infer earlier annual history. A pair with no successful fetch by `at` gives no_value (not_archived if never planned). Calendar reads use market:US; other endpoints use symbol. New financial_reports are summaries and do not guarantee TBVPS, finance-lease additions or segment revenue. Daily bars require exact trade_date alignment; never substitute an older benchmark session. New endpoint history starts with its own capture, never with a report period or a bar trade date.

exposes_tools.name: capture_status
exposes_tools.description: The archive's health now: ok, attention or failing, every reason, how the last capture start ended, and the last 7 runs with their pair counts (ok, tried with no ok, not tried, planned) and index membership. failing: a recent run ended partial or degraded (fewer than half its pairs ok) and no later day has ended complete since, missed days included; the last start had no usable token or stopped on a fatal error; no start has recorded its exit for longer than the configured bound; or the archive cannot be read. attention: a partial or degraded run that a later complete day followed, a recent day was missed, a run ended complete with pairs that have no ok, the latest universe is not observed, or the missed-day scan was incomplete. Reads local files only.

exposes_tools.name: read_at
exposes_tools.description: What the archive held at a past moment: for each read, the body of the latest successful fetch of that symbol and endpoint at or before `at`, at the JSON pointer. A later fetch is invisible, a failed fetch never replaces an earlier value, and an empty-shaped body is a value. Each read answers result value (with as_of, the capture's trading day, and fetched_at, UTC), not_archived (the archive never planned this symbol and endpoint), no_value (planned, but nothing fetched by `at`; the original six endpoints began capture 2026-10-13 UTC, for trading day 2026-10-12; annual starts only with its own first capture) or pointer_missing (the body has nothing at the pointer). Bodies are large (consensus ~20 KB, forecast_eps ~26 KB, rating_detail ~51 KB, valuation ~14 KB); an answer over 40 KiB fails with each read's size, so select with a pointer. Body shapes: consensus (default quarterly) and consensus_annual (period_type=af) {list[{fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_text, details[{key, name, estimate, actual, ...}]}], current_index, currency, opt_periods, current_period}; forecast_eps {items[{forecast_eps_median, forecast_eps_mean, forecast_eps_lowest, forecast_eps_highest, institution_total, institution_up, institution_down, forecast_start_date, forecast_end_date}]}; rating_latest {evaluate{buy, over, hold, under, sell, no_opinion, total, start_date, end_date}, target{highest_price, lowest_price, prev_close, start_date, end_date}, industry_*}; ratings {evaluate{strong_buy, buy, hold, sell, under, date}, recommend, target, change, ccy_symbol, updated_at}; rating_detail {evaluate{list[{strong_buy, buy, hold, sell, under, no_opinion, date}]}, target{updated_at, prediction_accuracy, data_percent, list[{timestamp, price, meet, avg_target, min_target, max_target, date}]}, ccy_symbol}; valuation {metrics{pe{low, median, high, desc, list[...]}}, range}. Reads local files only. New endpoints: earnings_snapshot {report, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, fp_start, fp_end, currency, fo_revenue, fo_ebit, fo_eps, fr_*}; financial_reports {report, symbol, list{IS,BS,CF}}, each kind has indicators[].accounts[{field,name,values[{year,fp_end,period,value,...}]}]. These are standardized summaries, not full filings; absent TBVPS, lease additions or segments must not be invented. daily_candlesticks is a typed projection {format:daily_bars_v1, symbol, timezone:America/New_York, adjust:none, session:regular, start,end,bars[{trade_date,timestamp,open,high,low,close,volume,turnover}]}; prices are decimal strings, at most six closes. Read stock and benchmark in one call, align by trade_date, report missing sessions. finance_calendar uses market:US instead of symbol and returns {format:earnings_calendar_v1,market,start,end,days{YYYY-MM-DD:{SYMBOL:{EVENT_ID:event}}},pages[{date,offset,fetched_at,raw_json}]}; select /days/YYYY-MM-DD/SYMBOL for a small answer. Empty calendar days are explicit. New data begins only with its first successful capture. Daily snapshots can precede later upstream earnings updates.

at.description: The moment to read at: an RFC 3339 time with an offset, such as 2026-10-13T16:00:00-04:00.

symbol.description: The security symbol as archived, such as NVDA.US.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON pointer into the body, such as /target/highest_price; "" for the whole body.

market.description: Market target for finance_calendar; omit symbol.

exposes_tools.name: capture_watch
exposes_tools.description: Start (on: true) or stop (on: false) keeping the live archive.status table on the calling Track. The table refreshes on the plugin's own poll, only when the status changes; stopping deletes it from this Track.

on.description: true to show the table on this Track, false to remove it

data_dir.description: Absolute path of the capture job's data dir (its config's data_dir). The plugin reads archive.sqlite3 read-only and last_exit.json there, and nothing else.

poll_seconds.description: Seconds between status reads for watching Tracks (10 to 3600).

stale_after_minutes.description: Minutes after the last recorded capture exit at which the status says the timer is not starting the capture (60 to 2880). It must exceed 30 (the timer's interval) plus the capture's attempt_timeout_minutes, with a margin: a start can hold the lock that long, and a start that finds the lock held records nothing. The default 90 fits attempt_timeout_minutes up to about 45.
